theme: glassblower's cooling schedules decide the final color
title: The Glassblower's Hysteresis Loop
strategies: constant prediction (mean of training measurements, ignores temperature) -> reproduces the checker baseline ~0.1

greedy: 1-D two-segment least-squares changepoint fit of final color on ENDPOINT temperature; fits monotone training data almost perfectly (path and endpoint are confounded there) but implicitly sets T_down==T_up (zero-width hysteresis / no branch memory) -> wrong on every held-out protocol that reheats into the bistable window without crossing the true upper spinodal

strong: same changepoint fit for the two branch curves and the lower spinodal, but explicitly POSITS a nonzero hysteresis loop (T_up = T_down_hat + a margin derived from the observed temperature span) so the grader's path rollout carries branch memory through reheats instead of re-deciding the branch from the endpoint alone

headroom above strong: the upper spinodal is never directly exercised by monotone-only training data, so a fixed-fraction margin heuristic is only approximately right; recovering T_up more precisely (e.g. from the training branch curves' extrapolated stability limits, or from any residual structure near the window) would close more of the remaining gap
